# Source origin

Repository: https://github.com/openssl/openssl

Revision: openssl-3.5.9

OpenSSL 3.5.9, whose `libcrypto` OTP's `crypto` links, imported as
erXos's code ([design-crypto.md](../docs/design-crypto.md#building-openssl)).
The files were taken from the release tarball
`https://github.com/openssl/openssl/releases/download/openssl-3.5.9/openssl-3.5.9.tar.gz`,
whose SHA-256, `archive_sha256` below
(`603f5602e2eef00d77fbd429d34dcd5822bb301757a1bc9cdb24c670f1eb859a`),
matches the release's published `openssl-3.5.9.tar.gz.sha256` and the
pin in `deps.lock`. `ruby tools/import_origins.rb --component openssl`
checked the tarball against that hash, compared the tree with it file by
file, removed the exclusions of `config/imports/openssl.json` and wrote
this record. Each imported file's SHA-256 is its row of the inventory.

Kept: every file of the release's `openssl-3.5.9/` directory outside the
exclusions, so that OpenSSL's `Configure`, the top-level `build.info` and
every `build.info` beneath it run unedited under erXos's configuration.
Left out: `test/`, `demos/`, `engines/`, `os-dep/`, `VMS/` and `ms/`, which
that configuration never reads, and the release's seven empty
directories; the inventory's `exclusions` give each reason.

License: Apache-2.0, whose text is `LICENSE.txt`. The release's sources
carry the OpenSSL Project's Apache-2.0 notice; the few that
also carry a co-author's BSD, CC0 or public-domain grant keep it in their
header. `external/perl/Text-Template-1.56/` is under the terms of Perl 5
(Artistic-1.0-Perl or GPL-1.0-or-later); it is a Perl module `Configure`
runs on the build host and is never compiled into `libcrypto`. erXos's
changes are under Apache-2.0.

Each file erXos changes says so in a `Modified by erXos` notice at its
top, which lists the changes. Two are changed, each taking FreeBSD's
branch under `__erxos__`, which erXos's target defines
([design-crypto.md](../docs/design-crypto.md#building-openssl)):

* `crypto/armcap.c` defines `OSSL_IMPLEMENT_GETAUXVAL` under `__erxos__`,
  so CPU features come from musl's `getauxval(AT_HWCAP)` and `AT_HWCAP2`,
  and the `SIGILL` probe is never compiled.
* `providers/implementations/rands/seeding/rand_unix.c` includes
  `<sys/random.h>` and, in `syscall_random`, skips the weak `getentropy`
  lookup and returns `getrandom(buf, buflen, 0)` under `__erxos__`.

erXos builds the tree with OpenSSL's own `Configure` and make, for its
target `config/openssl/erxos-aarch64.conf`, through
`tools/erx build openssl` (`tools/lib/erx/libcrypto.rb`).

The inventory records the imported bytes and their license evidence.
Third-party notices remain in their original files.
